boundary: Real AppState startup consumes and retains a separately authenticated console_auth_rt pool, verifies same observed database target, preserves the legacy business pool. Account fence/session activation and production/HA remain outside this transport boundary.

existing_owners.observation: validate_database_url_identity is the one current strict parser. No parse_auth_database_url or normalized target structure exists. It decodes effective password, rejects ambiguous/override DSN syntax and ambient PGOPTIONS, but returns String credential only. Do not fork parser or expand its query syntax for this lane.

connect_command_pool already creates max2/acquire3s pool, validates direct session_user/current_user/NOLOGIN-owner membership exclusions and fixed serving timeouts on connect and after reset/release, then independently validates pooled connection.

from_config creates runtime pool/custody verification then command pools before Self::new and later realtime/mail/bridge work. Auth connection and target refusal belong before usable AppState/background work.
new currently constructs AuthRestState from business pool; business pool serves Company/RLS legacy lookups and cannot be replaced by restricted auth pool.

AuthRestState currently stores only pool and services. Existing direct constructors also occur in group_admin_tenant_context and dev_auth_session integration tests; additive builder preserves those constructors while making new injected dependency explicit.

mechanical_steps: Only open auth transport for API + actual business DB + auth_rest configuration, matching existing requirement. Migrate/worker/no-DB/disabled-auth startup keeps current behavior; never substitute business pool for missing auth pool.

Call existing connect_command_pool(auth_url, console_auth_rt, AUTH_DATABASE_URL). Keep its existing role, membership, timeout and reset invariants. A private/auth-specific call-site map_err to a fixed AUTH_DATABASE_URL startup error is sufficient for credential redaction; do not stringify arbitrary driver details into errors. Alternatively add fixed env-key wrapping inside responsible shared helper if sibling behavior/tests demand it.

Bind target via actual public PostgreSQL metadata on both retained business/auth connections. Suggested minimal readback tuple: current_database() text, pg_database.oid bigint, inet_server_addr() text, inet_server_port(). Require equal non-null TCP endpoint and same DB name/OID; query error or missing row refuses. This is same-observed-server/database admission, not immutable physical-cluster authority.

Retain pool as an AppState auth_database dependency; AuthRestState must also retain the clone installed through a dedicated builder because its router receives a clone and its actual forthcoming legacy-fence readers need restricted access. Do not open/validate then discard pool, store only URL, or wrap the business pool under an auth label.

Assign dependencies before background consumers start. Keep AuthRestState.pool as legacy business pool. This transport-only change does not swap legacy passkey/refresh stores onto auth credentials (their Company tables still require business privileges).

When next fence lane is admitted, consume retained auth dependency in the shared request-context resolution and auth-rest prewrite owners; absence must fail closed for activated Account paths. AppState retention supports SSR/domain middleware/WS consumers outside AuthRestState. Do not claim storing a clone already enforces request fencing.

Run exact appended credential test and existing two transport tests after projection37 prerequisite; require direct correct authentication, direct wrong password28P01 and startup positive before desired runtime refusal. Then preserve config/parser and serving reset/identity regressions.

target_binding_tradeoff.recommended: Compare live observed endpoint/database metadata rather than raw host spelling. Existing allowed scheme aliases, percent-encoded database names, application_name and TLS/password query choices remain parser-owned and unchanged.
target_binding_tradeoff.accepted_aliases: Hostnames/IP spellings reaching the same observed server address/port and database satisfy this comparison without a hardcoded host allowlist.
target_binding_tradeoff.operating_limit: IPv4/IPv6 routes, proxies, multi-address listeners or primary/replica paths can report differing server endpoints even for one logical cluster. This minimal admission refuses differing observed endpoints; it does not promise support for every alias/topology.
target_binding_tradeoff.not_proven: Matching local endpoint+database OID/name can coincide across clusters, proxies or restored copies. No physical cluster identity, serving epoch, HA failover, replication freshness or current-session revocation guarantee follows.
rejected_shortcuts: Raw AUTH_DATABASE_URL == DATABASE_URL comparison includes deliberately different credentials
Raw hostname equality rejects benign aliases while not proving physical destination
Database name/OID alone can collide across clusters
Opening wrong database then interpreting missing fence as absent subject
Granting pg_control_system or owner access merely to manufacture stronger evidence
target_binding_tradeoff.later_authority: Immutable operator-provided deployment/serving identity and restore/failover generations remain the separately reviewed current-context/HA contract. Do not generate a startup nonce table or add migration/grants in this bounded transport lane.

stop_conditions: Implementation requires material new target trust contract or new privileges
Pool is validated but discarded or not retained for the responsible auth consumer
